proof_summary: Lucas’s parity criterion converts oddness of the two binomial factors into disjointness conditions on binary digits, which show that each odd summand indexed by \((n,k)\), with \(j=(N-n(k+1))/(n+1)\), is paired involutively with the summand indexed by \((j+k,k)\). Any fixed point forces \(j=0\) and \(n=k\), hence \(N=k(k+1)\); otherwise all odd summands cancel in pairs modulo \(2\).
